record.title: EmbodiedMemory-Bench reports simulation results for action-outcome memory
record.summary: The EmbodiedMemory-Bench preprint evaluates memory methods over 2,554 interactive episodes in four embodied-task families. The authors report matched-backbone comparisons for external action-outcome memory and show that adding maximal historical RGB context can reduce Gemini-3-Flash average success by 10.4 percentage points in the reported comparison. The results are primarily from simulation; the Robotics-ER subset is limited to 10% because of API instability. The paper does not establish physical-robot performance, independent reproduction or deployment benefit.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In Table 2, the authors report that adding maximal historical RGB context lowers Gemini-3-Flash average success rate by 10.4 percentage points in the reported comparison; the paper also reports task-specific gains for its external action-outcome memory under matched-backbone comparisons.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The paper describes evaluation as primarily simulated and reports that Robotics-ER coverage was reduced to a 10% subset because of API instability; physical-robot performance is not established.

evidence_gaps.description: The author-reported matched-backbone benchmark results have not been independently reproduced.
Most reported evaluation is simulated, and the Robotics-ER subset covers only 10% due to API instability; physical-robot performance and transfer are unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported benchmark comparisons hold, task-specific action-outcome memory can outperform simply accumulating raw multimodal history in some simulated embodied-agent tasks, affecting memory design and evaluation for long-horizon agents. The paper does not establish physical-robot performance or broad transfer.
limitations: Results are reported by the paper authors and have not been independently reproduced.
Evaluation is primarily simulated; the paper does not establish physical-robot performance or deployment benefit.
Robotics-ER uses a 10% subset because of API instability, limiting coverage of that task family.
Task-specific matched-backbone results do not establish that action-outcome memory is superior across all tasks, models or memory budgets.

technical.claimed_result: The paper evaluates 2,554 interactive episodes in four task families. Its Table 2 reports task-specific matched-backbone comparisons for external action-outcome memory and reports a 10.4-point average-success decrease for Gemini-3-Flash when maximal historical RGB context is added.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible preprint documents its benchmark, methods and author-reported results. the research desk did not independently reproduce them.
technical.mechanism: External memory records action-outcome information for retrieval during embodied tasks; the benchmark compares this approach with alternative memory/context conditions, including accumulated visual history.
technical.novelty: A multi-task embodied-agent memory benchmark with matched-backbone comparisons that distinguishes structured action-outcome memory from raw multimodal context accumulation.
technical.regime: 2,554 interactive episodes across four task families, primarily simulated. Robotics-ER is represented by a 10% subset due to API instability. Reported results are bounded to the paper's tasks, models and memory configurations.
technical.reproducibility: The preprint provides benchmark and comparison descriptions. No independent reproduction was performed; physical-robot performance is not established.
technical.strongest_baseline: Matched-backbone memory/context conditions in Table 2. The paper's results are task-specific and do not show universal superiority across all tasks or memory budgets.

brief.title: EmbodiedMemory-Bench reports simulation results for action-outcome memory
brief.why_it_matters: The benchmark makes a concrete comparison between structured action-outcome memory and raw multimodal history in embodied-agent tasks. If the task-scoped results reproduce, they could guide memory-system design and evaluation. The result is simulation-bounded and does not support a physical deployment claim.
